title: Michael Clayton
events_chronological: Arthur Edens, lead counsel on a six-year class action defending the agrochemical company U-North, stops taking his medication.
Arthur strips during a deposition in Milwaukee and runs into the car park announcing that he is a servant of a corrupt design.
Michael Clayton, the firm's fixer and a ruined gambler, is sent to Milwaukee to bring Arthur back.
Michael, in debt to loan sharks over a failed restaurant, asks his firm for a loan against his bonus and is refused.
Karen Crowder, U-North's general counsel, is briefed about Arthur and rehearses her answers alone in a hotel bathroom.
Arthur has obtained an internal memorandum showing that U-North knew its weedkiller was killing people.
Arthur telephones a plaintiff in the case and orders six hundred bound copies of the memorandum printed.
Karen authorises two contractors to put Arthur under full surveillance.
The contractors kill Arthur in his flat and stage it as a suicide by injection.
Michael refuses to accept the suicide and finds the printer's receipt among Arthur's things.
Michael's brother's debts and his son's telephone calls close in on him from every direction at once.
Michael collects Arthur's annotated copy of the memorandum from the printers.
The contractors put a device in Michael's car while he has stopped at the roadside to look at three horses in a field.
The car explodes, and Michael throws his watch and rings into the fire so that the body will be taken for his.
Michael confronts Karen at a U-North board meeting, records her offering him money to keep quiet, and has the police waiting in the lobby.
Michael gets into a taxi, hands the driver fifty dollars and tells him to just drive.
syuzhet_notes: The film opens on the last night - the horses, the device, the explosion - and then a caption reading four days earlier sends it back to the beginning, after which it runs forward until it catches up with the fire.
fabula_notes: The dead lawyer's voice is heard over the opening, but it is a message left on an answering machine and belongs to a scene inside the chronology rather than to a frame outside it.
